newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU jobs bonanza may not be so big after all.
newsitem.headline: EU jobs bonanza may not be so big after all.

text.p: After late night wrangling by ministers and top-level political brinkmanship by its leaders, the European Union is committing itself to a new plan to boost employment across the bloc.
But a top British official has answered the question on everyone's lips. How many jobs will actually be created?

The aide to Prime Minister Tony Blair shot out the number in response to repeated questioning from a journalist who recently stood -- and was defeated -- as a parliamentary candidate for the Conservative party, the Daily Telegraph's Boris Johnson.

British officials -- who have been stressing that Blair backs Europe's new emphasis on jobs but is opposed to French socialist ideas that EU funds should be spent to create them -- said later the answer was intended to be flippant.
But in the same spirit, columnists suggested that Britain's new Labour government -- unused to the ways of European summits -- might in fact have let slip a jealously guarded secret.
